glosses: to allow, to permit

examples.text: Позво́льте мне я́сно заяви́ть.
— Позво́льте мне сего́дня пойти́ в го́сти, — сказа́ла одна́жды На́стя, одева́я ба́рышню.
examples.translation: “Allow me to go visiting today,” Nastya said one day as she was dressing the young lady.
examples.english: “Allow me to go visiting today,” Nastya said one day as she was dressing the young lady.

glosses: to afford (often as позволить себе)
excuse (me), sorry, pardon (me) (used to express objection, disagreement or reminding of some fact)

examples.text: Позво́льте, но ра́зве не э́тим и до́лжен занима́ться сове́т?
examples.translation: Excuse me, but isn't that what the council should be doing?
examples.english: Excuse me, but isn't that what the council should be doing?

examples.text: Позво́льте, а почему́ могло́ бы быть хорошо́?

examples.text: — Позво́льте. Кро́ме того́, вы, как и вся ва́ша коми́ссия, си́льно скомпромети́рованы. Вы без вся́кого обеспе́чения взя́ли из ба́нка 19 ты́сяч.
examples.translation: "Excuse me. Apart from that you and your committee are seriously compromised. You borrowed nineteen thousand from the bank, giving no security."
examples.english: "Excuse me. Apart from that you and your committee are seriously compromised. You borrowed nineteen thousand from the bank, giving no security."

glosses: дать разрешение, выразить согласие на совершение какого-либо действия
дать возможность сделать что-либо
To let one have as a suitable share of something.

examples.text: to allow a servant his liberty; to allow a free passage; to allow one day for rest

glosses: To permit, to give permission to.

examples.text: I will allow my son to be absent.

glosses: To not bar or obstruct.

examples.text: Although I don't consent to their holding such meetings, I will allow them for the time being.

glosses: To acknowledge, accept the truth of; to concede; to accede to an opinion.

examples.text: to allow a right; to allow a claim; to allow an appeal
You must allow that disagreeing about politics puts a strain on a relationship.
Mr. Knightley, I shall not allow you to be a fair judge in this case.
I allow, with Mrs. Grundy and most moralists, that Miss Newcome's conduct[…]was highly reprehensible.
Half the night passed before the wench allowed that it might be safe to stop.

glosses: To grant (something) as a deduction or an addition; especially to abate or deduct.

examples.text: to allow a sum for leakage

glosses: To make an allowance, to take into account when making plans.

examples.text: When calculating a budget for a construction project, always allow for contingencies.

glosses: To render physically possible.

examples.text: The inlet allowed a facility to bring the money in a boat secretly and at night to the very foot of the hill.

glosses: To praise; to approve of; hence, to sanction.

examples.text: Truly ye bear witness that ye allow the deeds of your fathers

glosses: To sanction; to invest; to entrust.

examples.text:

glosses: To like; to be suited or pleased with.

examples.text: How allow you the model of these clothes?

examples.text: Mr. Cooke at once began a tirade against the residents of Asquith for permitting a sandy and generally disgraceful condition of the roads. glosses: To allow (someone) to do something; to give permission to.

examples.text: He was ultimately cleared, but during that period, Mr. Ackman said, his lawyers would not permit him to defend himself publicly.

glosses: To allow for, to make something possible.

examples.text: What was left to say? Quite a lot, if only parliamentary time permitted.

examples.text: We've been busy permitting the State Street development.

glosses: To hand over, resign (something to someone).

examples.text: Let us not aggravate our sorrows, / But to the gods permit the event of things.
